Typical symptoms of GERD are heartburn and regurgitation of gastric contents into the oropharynx [1]. GERD affects quality of life and may cause erosive esophagitis, esophageal strictures, and Barrett esophagus, a precursor to esophageal adenocarcinoma [1]. Symptoms potentially attributable to gastroesophageal reflux disease are among those most commonly reported to primary care providers in the outpatient setting [2]. 

## Management and Treatment
GERD is a clinical diagnosis and is most effectively treated with proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs) [1]. Long-term use of PPIs is associated with bone fractures, chronic renal disease, acute renal disease, community-acquired pneumonia, and Clostridium difficile intestinal infection [1].
